instruction: In the stone bridge that carries the canal over the ravine, in the arch nearest the sunset, the one shut with rough stones: on the side facing upstream, at the foot of the pier, 3 cubits: [deposit].
context: Redacted site description: a stone-built canal bridge of the early first millennium BCE that carries an irrigation canal across a shallow valley. It is more than 280 m long and 22 m wide; near the middle a stream runs under a row of five corbelled arches. Floods breached the middle of the structure. Excavators cleared the faces and the arch piers in one short season.

features.type: corbelled pointed archway over the stream

position.relative_to: centre of the arch bay (stream crossing)

features.notes: Second arch from the west; lower courses of its piers survive. Two curved stones from a pier breakwater, one inscribed, were found wedged in its mouth. No blocking recorded.

position.relative_to: west end of the structure, top

features.notes: Large area of concrete bedding with small patches of stone pavement still in place; remains of the canal parapet.

features.type: corbelled pointed archway over the stream

position.relative_to: centre of the arch bay (stream crossing)

features.dimensions: stands six courses high; courses about 0.50 m
features.notes: Westernmost of the five arches. Partly blocked by a rough wall. The pavement under the piers is of large stones laid diagonally to the flow.

features.type: repaired section of the outer face

position.relative_to: west end of the structure, south face

features.dimensions: about 45 m long (first three bays from the west)
features.notes: Ancient repair of a breach: base courses project and step back course by course; irregular filling of re-used blocks, many carrying parts of another inscription.

features.type: corbelled pointed archway over the stream (not preserved)

position.relative_to: centre of the arch bay (stream crossing)

features.notes: Easternmost of the five arches. Carried away by the central breach together with most of the foundation platform.
